text.p: On overnight commodity markets, copper and aluminium prices surged as traders looked ahead at tight supply developing around certain delivery dates.
Gold futures rose sharply and bullion prices firmed, due largely to the fall in the U.S. dollar on Thursday.
Oil prices rose with heating oil while wheat prices rose on short covering.
The CRB Index rose 1.71 points to 238.74.

METALS - Copper and aluminium prices held gains in late inter-office activity after soaring on Thursday on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on tightness that traders saw developing around certain delivery dates. Three months delivery copper ended the kerb $46 a tonne higher at $2,017 and was bid at $2,016 by the time Comex ended at 1900 GMT. At that hour aluminium was also assessed just firmer from the end of the kerb when it had stood $33 higher from Wednesday at $1,466.50. This was a two-month high and the day's peak. Traders said the late drive higher in copper prices coincided with a further widening in the cash/threes backwardation to over $60 from below $50 on
Wednesday. This seemed to signal another sizeable drawdown in LME stocks on Friday.

GOLD - New York precious metals futures were sharply higher midday Thursday, led by silver, as a shortcovering rally by funds pushed up the complex, traders said. "It looks to be mostly dollar related, though base metals are up also on prompt market tightness and buying by under hedged consumer users," Merrill Lynch commodity strategist Bill O'Neill said. The sharp fall in the dollar Thursday unnerved world stock and bond markets but is seen beneficial for Asian demand for metals

depressed by the dollar's rise in the past year. COMEX December gold was up $2.60 at $381.30 an ounce, after seeing a morning high at $382.00. Spot gold in the bullion market was quoted $380.30/380.80 an ounce, up from the London Thursday afternoon fix at $378.60, and the New York close Wednesday at $377.70/378.20, after gold saw a 19 month low at $376.80 seen last week.

OIL - NYMEX crude oil prices followed heating oil up Thursday, but crude's gains were capped by adequate supply levels seen in recent inventory data, traders said. "Crude seems to be kicking and screaming as it follows heating oil up. Crude took the market off its highs because of the APIs," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products at Paribas Futures Inc. At 1045 EST December crude was 13 cents up at $22.82 a barrel while December heating oil was 0.90 cent higher a gallon at 67.35 cents. The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday that crude stocks grew 9.3 million barrels.

GRAIN - CBOT wheat futures were higher at midsession on short covering plus an EU export rebate that was not as steep as some had expected, traders said. The EU Thursday granted 22.35 ECUs for wheat exports. Some had expected the subsidy to total 25 ECUs. Support also came from USDA's weekly export sales report which showed U.S. net wheat export sales for the week ending October 31 at 453,300 tonnes. That tally was near expectations for 500,000 tonnes, traders said. News that Turkey may be importing 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat to curb high bread prices also may have lent support.
